chapter_name: Social Responsibilities of Business and Business Ethics
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand that business is not just about making money! Learn why businesses must care for the environment, society, and ethical principles.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It is the obligation of a business to take actions that protect and improve the welfare of society as a whole, along with making profits. A business uses society's resources, so it must give back!
A business must be responsible to its Shareholders (fair returns), Workers (safe environment, fair wages), Consumers (good quality, no false ads), and Government (paying taxes honestly).

Industrialization causes air, water, land, and noise pollution. Businesses must adopt eco-friendly technologies, safely dispose of waste, and comply with government pollution norms to save the planet.
Ethics refers to deciding what is morally 'right' and 'wrong' in business conduct. It involves fair practices, honesty, and avoiding adulteration, black marketing, or exploiting workers.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ The CEO's Dilemma
fun_activity.instructions: You are the CEO of a toy company. You find out a cheap chemical you use to paint toys might cause allergies in 1% of children. It's totally legal in your country, and changing it will cost millions. What do you do? (Hint: Business Ethics says drop the chemical immediately!)

exam_tips: 📌 Always frame the 'Arguments for Social Responsibility' around long-term survival, public image, and avoiding government regulation.
📌 Learn the difference between legal responsibility (what the law demands) and social responsibility (voluntary actions beyond the law).
📌 When writing about Business Ethics, mention elements like top management commitment, code of conduct, and employee involvement.
quick_recap: ⭐ The 'Iron Law of Responsibility' states that in the long run, those who do not use power in a manner society considers responsible will lose it.
⭐ Protecting the environment is not just an ethical duty but also a legal requirement for businesses today.
⭐ Top management plays the most crucial role in guiding an entire organization toward ethical behavior.
